content.text:
I added the `version` subcommand, registered it in `internal/cmds/registry.go`, and added tests. `go vet ./...` and `go test ./...` both pass.

It reports the app name `app`, the build version (default `dev`) and `runtime.Version()`. To set the version at build time, use `-ldflags "-X example.com/app/internal/cmds.BuildVersion=1.2.3"`.

I did not copy the existing commands in two ways, because the project rules forbid printing under `internal/`. `status.go` prints with `fmt.Printf`. `version` instead logs through `internal/log`, so the output goes to stderr in slog text format, not stdout. Extra arguments produce a warning and are otherwise ignored, as in `status`.

`BuildVersion` is a package-level `var`, because `-ldflags -X` can only set a variable. That conflicts with the "no package-level mutable state" rule. I don't see a way around it, and I kept it to that one variable.

The tests are in `internal/cmds/version_test.go`. They are table-driven and cover the reported fields, the `Version` return value with and without arguments, the `dev` default, and the registry entry. They don't capture the log output itself.
